newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB sees demand picking up in 1998.
newsitem.headline: ABB sees demand picking up in 1998.

text.p: ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG expects demand to pick up in Western Europe in 1998, while 1997 is likely to stay sluggish.
ABB chairman Percy Barnevik said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television that it could still be some time before demand for capital goods takes hold within the current business cycle.

"Even if you hope that 1997 will see an increased demand for consumer products, investment goods come later in the cycle. I hope 1998 will be a better demand year, but I don't have any hopes for 1997 for an upturn for investment goods," he said.
Regarding the concern's worldwide activities, he said that Russia and the former Soviet bloc countries are moving at different paces, but in most cases progress was slow.
"We have 8,000 people in Russia, including minority companies --about 20 of them. I would say half of them are making a profit now," Barnevik said.
He said progress could be quicker in some of those countries, but it may take up to five years in Russia.
Barnevik acknowledged that he was not satisfied with the pace.
But he added: "As long as you make steady progress, even slow, you have to live with that."
He said that business in South America was favourable, naming specifically Argentina, Chile and Colombia.
"We think we can double our business there in the next five or six years," he said.
He also was optimistic about India, which he said was likely to see growth in demand similar to that in China.
"With the reform policy in India... opening up the financial markets, India is very attractive," he said.
